info.longBusinessSummary: Vale S.A., together with its subsidiaries, produces iron ore and nickel in Brazil, Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Oceania. The company operates in two segments, Iron Ore Solutions and Vale Base Metals. It extracts, produces, and distributes iron ore, iron ore pellets, briquettes, nickel, copper, other ferrous products, and by-products, including gold, silver, cobalt, platinum-group metals, and other base metals, as well as low-carbon critical minerals. The company also operates logistics systems and distribution centers, such as mining complexes, railways, and maritime terminals, ports, and ships; generates energy from hydroelectric, solar, and wind sources; and engages in greenfield mineral exploration. In addition, it is involved in research; and trading activities. The company was formerly known as Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and changed its name to Vale S.A. in May 2009. Vale S.A. was founded in 1942 and is headquartered in Rio De Janeiro, Brazil.

and a continued focus on operational excellence. In a dynamic market environment, our portfolio flexibility, affreightment strategy, and
hedging program helped protect margins and support solid cash flow generation, further strengthening our balance sheet. In iron ore, we

gain momentum, with Salobo delivering record third-quarter production and both copper and nickel on track to reach the upper half of the
production guidances. With the approval of the Salobo CPF project, we take another important step in our copper growth journey, leveraging

growth projects. Pellet production totaled 8.6 Mt (+7% y/y). • Based on year-to-date performance and expected operational improvements,
Vale remains confident in delivering the lower end of its iron ore production guidance (335-345 Mt) and the midpoint of its pellet production
guidance (30-34 Mt) for 2026. • The Compact Crushing project started operation in Q3. Together with the ramp-up of the Serra Sul
+20 project, it is expected to enhance operational flexibility and support performance from 2027. • The operations at Fábrica
mine resumed in September, following compliance with applicable safety, environmental, and licensing requirements, as well as actions
established under the Commitment Agreement. Vale Base Metals • Copper production totaled 85.5 kt (-6% y/y), reflecting the planned
SAG mill rebuild at Sossego, partly offset by strong performance at Salobo. Nickel output totaled 49.7 kt (6% y/y), driven mainly by the
strong performance at Onça Puma's second furnace and the highest quarterly output at the Sudbury Refinery since 4Q13. • Vale
is on track to achieve the upper half of its 2026 production guidance ranges for both copper (360-380 kt) and nickel (185-200 kt). Year-to-date,
